items.note: Page (last updated 22 March 2026) states circulation and parking banned 7:30-10:30 on weekdays, Saturday excluded; cameras at 27 entry points and 11 internal points where other limits apply; public-transport streets closed 7:00-20:00 every day incl. holidays; Area Romana closed 21:00-7:30. Title matches.

Page (25 March 2026) confirms the Giunta approved the delibera on 24 March 2026 extending ZTL Valentino to viale Medaglie d'Oro and the northern stretch of viale Ceppi with new camera gates, activation subject to MIT authorisation, and about 90 blue-line spaces as a temporary solution until a new underground car park of almost 500 spaces in 'Padiglione V' opens. The page does not mention Torino Esposizioni; that identification is not on the source.
items.corrected_text: On 24 March 2026 the city's executive approved extending the ZTL Valentino to viale Medaglie d'Oro and the northern part of viale Ceppi with new camera gates, whose activation needs ministry authorisation. About 90 blue-line spaces on viale Medaglie d'Oro serve as a temporary solution until works end and a new underground car park of almost 500 spaces in Padiglione V opens.

items.note: Page (8 July 2025) says the Region welcomed approval in the Chamber's Environment Committee of an amendment that moves the Euro 5 diesel ban to 1 October 2026 and applies it primarily to cities above 100,000 inhabitants; assessor Marnati said compensatory measures would allow Euro 5 diesels to keep running in Torino and Novara too. The page does not give the previous 1 October 2025 date or call the ban 'structural', and the amendment had only passed committee, so 'moved' as a done national change overstates its status.
items.corrected_text: The Piedmont Region welcomed the approval, in the Chamber of Deputies' environment committee, of an amendment shifting the Euro 5 diesel ban to 1 October 2026 and applying it primarily to cities above 100,000 inhabitants. The Region said compensatory measures would allow Euro 5 diesels to keep running in Torino and Novara as well.

items.note: Source is an ANCE Torino circular (PDF, 2 July 2026), not a Region statement. It says the Piedmont Region managed to avoid the Euro 5 diesel ban that could have applied from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027 in municipalities above 100,000 inhabitants (Torino and Novara), by adopting compensatory measures in the regional air-quality plan. Facts match; only the attribution 'Piedmont reported' is wrong.
items.corrected_text: A July 2026 ANCE Torino circular reported that the Piedmont Region had avoided the Euro 5 diesel circulation ban that could have applied from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027 in Torino and Novara, by adopting compensatory measures in its regional air-quality plan.

items.note: guidatorino.com page published 26 July 2023 with exactly this title. It says the city council approved the GTT tariff update presented in mid-July; strisce blu: smart 1 -> 1.20, ridotta 1.30 -> 1.50, ordinaria 1.50 -> 1.70, centrale 2.50 -> 2.80 euros/hour; resident parking subscriptions unchanged. Rates match exactly. Note: page says changes could take effect by 1 October 2023 (not confirmed in force on this page); single secondary source, though the 2026 sicurauto guide (item 5) shows the same rates in force.

Page (30 January 2026) lists 2.80 ZTL Centrale, 1.70 ordinaria, 1.50 ridotta, 1.20 smart; Monday-Saturday 8:00-19:30, free Sundays and holidays; resident permit 180 euros a year (250 for non-resident domiciled). The reduction applies with an ISEE showing household income below 50,000 euros, which the draft's 'low-income households' mischaracterises.
items.corrected_text: A 2026 guide lists on-street rates of 2.80 euros an hour in the ZTL Centrale, 1.70 ordinary, 1.50 reduced and 1.20 smart, charged Monday to Saturday 8:00-19:30 and free on Sundays and holidays. It gives the annual residents' permit as 180 euros, with a reduced rate for households with an ISEE-certified income below 50,000 euros.

items.note: City press release of 8 August 2025: ZTL suspended Mon 11 to Fri 22 August 2025, on-street paid parking 11 to 24 August 2025; parking still charged in automated (barrier) car parks and GTT-run structure car parks. Title matches.

Moveo article (19 November 2025): per a Giunta delibera, strisce blu in the whole Sottozona A chargeable on normally free Sundays/holidays 7, 8, 14 and 21 December 2025, 8:00-19:30, at the ZTL centrale rate of 2.80 euros/hour. Draft title matches the on-page headline (HTML <title> differs slightly).

City release (16 June 2026): in 'parcheggi convenzionati' (participating car parks) in the ZTL Centrale, the entry camera reads the plate during 7:30-10:30 weekday hours and after more than 30 minutes the plate is auto-added to the white list sent to 5T; trial (since 2018, resumed 2022) at Cernaia and Emanuele Filiberto; Giunta made it permanent for 5 years; operational start planned after the summer. The page limits this to participating car parks, not all structure/barrier car parks.
items.corrected_text: The city announced that drivers entering participating car parks inside the ZTL Centrale during restricted hours will no longer need a paper authorisation: an entry camera reads the plate and vehicles parked over 30 minutes are added automatically to the whitelist. The system was trialled at the Cernaia and Emanuele Filiberto car parks and made permanent for five years, with operational start planned after the summer.

items.note: GTT Rendicontazione di sostenibilita 2025, p.29: GTT manages on-street paid parking across Torino and 30 barrier, structure and residents' (pertinenziali) car parks in the centre and at main entry points, with a Park & Ride fare (day ticket or monthly pass). Revenue table: Sosta 47,209,836 euros (2025) vs 44,641,071 (2024), +5.75%.

GTT report p.122: 870 parking meters, per-minute payment via SostApp or third-party apps. Online channel table (euro mln, gross of VAT): GTT SostApp 2.8 (2023), 7.7 (2024), 10.1 (2025); Operatori App 11.2 in 2025.

HDmotori (12 November 2025) on the Motus-E report at 30 September 2025: provinces ranked Roma 5,881, Milano 4,970, Napoli 3,120, Torino 3,075 (+324 in 12 months), Brescia 1,843. Torino is fourth, not fifth.
items.corrected_text: Motus-E figures put the province of Torino at 3,075 public charging points as of 30 September 2025, 324 more than 12 months earlier, fourth among Italian provinces.

items.note: GTT report: total passengers 300,414,096 (2025) vs 286,420,934 (2024), +4.9%; paying urban trips rose from 257 to 264 million.

Regione Piemonte news (9 April 2026): '[I]Torino' closed 2025 with over 1.8 million arrivals and 4.7 million presenze (+6.3%, +6.7%); foreign movements +13% in both arrivals and presenze. Source text has a typo 'ITorino'; figures are distinct from the larger Turismo Torino e Provincia area (8m+ nights), consistent with the city.

QuiFinanza (20 November 2025): about 230,000 spectators, about double the first Torino edition in 2021 (figures given by FITP president Binaghi); total economic impact close to 600 million euros according to Boston Consulting Group studies linked to the event.

Infra.To press release dated 7 March 2026 says the preliminary activities 'will start' from Monday 9 March at 11 temporary sites (incl. Corso Vittorio Emanuele II at via Nizza and Piazza Carlo Alberto), each lasting about a week at most, with no permanent traffic changes. It announces a planned start; it does not confirm the work started. Title matches.
items.corrected_text: A metro line 2 press release of 7 March 2026 announced that preliminary environmental-monitoring work would start on 9 March 2026 at 11 temporary sites, including Corso Vittorio Emanuele II at via Nizza and Piazza Carlo Alberto. Each site was expected to last about a week, with no permanent traffic changes.

items.note: Mentelocale event page (marked 'Evento terminato', publication date not shown; byline 'Gemini Ai per mentelocale'): inauguration of the new pedestrian via Roma on Saturday 12 September 2026, after completion of works on the last stretch between Piazza Castello and Piazza Carlo Felice; works funded with 12 million euros from EU PN Metro Plus 2021-2027. Title matches. Caution: AI-written event listing, a primary city source would be stronger.

corrected_summary: Torino's ZTL Centrale bans circulation and parking for unauthorised vehicles on weekday mornings, and GTT manages on-street paid parking across the city plus 30 barrier, structure and residents' car parks; a 2023 GTT tariff update approved by the city council raised on-street hourly rates, which a 2026 guide lists at 1.20-2.80 euros. A 2025 amendment shifted the Euro 5 diesel ban to 1 October 2026, and in July 2026 the Piedmont Region was reported to have avoided it in Torino and Novara through compensatory measures; via Roma's pedestrianisation was inaugurated on 12 September 2026, and preliminary environmental-monitoring work for metro line 2 was announced to start in March 2026. GTT reports higher passenger numbers and parking revenue in 2025 than in 2024, and the Piedmont Region reports tourist arrivals and overnight stays in Torino grew in 2025.
